docs.summary: Something a build can be produced for.
docs.remarks: Registered data rather than an enum. A console cannot appear in a public enum in this repository, and a target is really a platform and an architecture together, which an enum of platform names cannot express. [`Id`](#api~Prowl.Editor.Build.PlatformTarget~Id) is the one value that must never change: it keys the asset variant cache and appears in the build manifest, so renaming one invalidates shipped output.

members.name: Id
members.signature: public required string Id { get; init; }

docs.summary: The unique identifier that keys the asset variant cache and appears in the build manifest. Must never change once shipped.

members.name: DisplayName
members.signature: public required string DisplayName { get; init; }

docs.summary: The human-readable name shown in the editor UI.

members.name: Family
members.signature: public required string Family { get; init; }

docs.summary: Grouping only, for example "desktop" or "mobile". A string so a new family needs no engine change.

members.name: RuntimeIdentifiers
members.signature: public required IReadOnlyList<string> RuntimeIdentifiers { get; init; }

docs.summary: The .NET runtime identifiers this target builds for.
docs.remarks: A list because several real targets are not one architecture. An Android App Bundle carries multiple ABIs in one artifact, and a macOS universal binary is built per architecture and merged.

members.name: Capabilities
members.signature: public required TargetCapabilities Capabilities { get; init; }

docs.summary: The capabilities this target supports, such as texture formats, graphics APIs, and feature flags.
The platform name assembly definitions and plugins are filtered by, when the target maps to one.
Preprocessor symbols always defined for this target.
